question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the Prime Broker engaged by a Category III AIF must be:

answer.text: Registered in India only — offshore prime brokers are prohibited.
A registered Portfolio Manager under SEBI (PM) Regulations, 2020.
Approved by the AIF trustee only — SEBI registration is irrelevant.
Registered with SEBI in India OR a recognised offshore prime broker.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit Category III AIFs to engage Prime Brokers that are either registered in India (typically with SEBI as brokers/custodians/bankers) OR recognised prime brokers offshore. This flexibility recognises the global nature of Cat III hedge fund strategies and the need for offshore PBs for cross-border trades, foreign-exchange, and global-macro exposures. The Trap: Option A invents an India-only restriction. Option B confuses PBs with Portfolio Managers. Option C drops the regulatory oversight requirement altogether. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests this from the Cat III distributor angle. Not tested in XIX-D (Cat I/II) — no PBs in those categories. Manager's Pro-Tip: When picking an offshore PB, verify 'recognised' status: home-regulator (FCA, SEC, MAS) registration plus ISDA/CSA master agreement readiness. Your legal will negotiate rehypothecation limits — cap it tight (e.g., 140% of debit) so a PB bankruptcy doesn't trap your long inventory.
